title: Best Buy Gift Card Fraud PSA
description: As gift cards have gotten more popular over the years, they're increasingly targeted by scammers as an easy way to steal money from innocent victims. That's why Best Buy teamed up with AARP and the National Association of Attorneys General to create a PSA to educate and empower customers to spot and stop gift card scams.

asr.full_text: Over the years, buying gift cards for loved ones has grown in popularity. Unfortunately, it's also become popular with scammers. You may get a call or an email from somebody pretending to be a family member in distress, or even the IRS. The scammer will ask you to go to purchase a gift card, often in the thousands of dollars. He'll then ask you for the number on the back of the card. And if you don't give it to him, he'll threaten your family members, may even threaten you lose jail time. You can contact the consumer protection division of your state attorney general's office and they will help you determine whether you are being scammed. These gift cards can only be used to buy products or services from the issue in retailer. They can not be used to pay bail, your taxes, or court rights. If you receive a call or email asking for payment by gift card, know that this is a scam. Help spread the word. Help stop the scam.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because its purpose is to educate viewers about gift-card fraud and help them identify and stop it. The purchase and card-number requests are presented as a hypothetical scam mechanism involving impersonated family members or the IRS, with the threats framed as warning signs rather than an audience offer. Interview framing and the closing “Spread the word” screen with consumer-protection organizations further support an awareness campaign context.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary theme is a warning about a depicted third-party mechanism involving impersonation, gift-card purchase, card-number disclosure, and threats. The source also directs viewers to consumer-protection assistance and describes the material as a PSA intended to help customers spot and stop gift-card scams.
